pages.quiz:
SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

5. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Glucose and oxygen

6. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.

8. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Paper burning to ash

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 0 °C

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. joule (J)

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

2. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

5. D — Glucose and oxygen

6. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

7. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

8. A — Ice melting to water

9. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

10. C — 100 °C

11. B — newton (N)

12. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Change of State; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Composition of Air; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Levers as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
